rounds.text: Tech Mahindra is demonstrably under-appreciated by those who overlook its surging operational profitability and structural margin expansion. Operating margins have climbed to 17% in the trailing twelve months, up 8 percentage points over three years, while quarterly operating margins reached 18% in September 2026, marking a 3 percentage point year-on-year gain [E30, E31]. This margin improvement is structural and backed by rigorous cost execution, with management firmly reiterating its path toward a full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% [E75]. Furthermore, profitability is fully realized in cash rather than accounting maneuvers, evidenced by a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.28x alongside ₹6,172 crores in operating cash flow and ₹5,626 crores in free cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. Commercial momentum strongly supports this earnings quality, highlighted by total last-12-month deal wins surging 34.8% year-on-year to US$4,270 million and new deal wins reaching US$1,023 million [E88, E89]. The balance sheet remains a fortress with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x and borrowings ticking down to ₹2,184 crores [E37, E39], enabling a shareholder-friendly capital allocation policy that includes a 1:1 bonus share issue and an interim dividend of ₹15 per share [E90, E91]. Conceded: the evidence shows a rich valuation with a P/E of 30.6x and a reverse DCF implying 14.4% earnings growth against a 2% base case, alongside past historical sales and profit growth challenges [E1, E16, E19, E47]. Nonetheless, the combination of surging TTM profit growth of 27%, dominant institutional confidence driving positive money flow, and upcoming catalysts like AI revenue reporting in H2 FY27 proves that the market is undervaluing the scale of this operational turnaround [E21, E44, E76].

Tech Mahindra trades at a rich valuation that severely disconnects from its underlying historical growth, sitting at a P/E of 30.6x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 5.88x [E2]. This lofty multiple is entirely unsupported by the company’s medium-term performance, given that compounded sales growth over the past three years limps at just 2% [E16] and compounded profit growth over the same span is an anemic 1% [E20]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation pegs intrinsic value at a meager Rs 724 per share against a market price of Rs 1,783, translating to a stark -146.2% margin of safety [E45, E46]. The reverse DCF reveals that today's market price already bakes in an aggressive 14.4% earnings growth expectation, towering over the 2.0% growth assumed in the base case [E47]. Institutional confidence is also quietly eroding, evidenced by foreign institutional investors trimming their holdings from 24.58% in December 2023 down to 20.76% by September 2026 [E42]. Conceded: operating margins have expanded to 17% in the TTM from 9% three years prior [E30], and the trailing twelve months show a strong rebound in profit growth to 27% [E21].

Conceded: 3-year sales growth is 2% [E16] and 3-year profit growth is 1% [E20]. However, the bear's backward-looking critique misses the explosive acceleration occurring right now in the business, evidenced by TTM profit growth surging to 27% [E21] and quarterly net profit jumping 34% year-on-year [E66]. While the bear highlights foreign institutional selling [E42], it completely ignores the massive accumulation by domestic institutions whose holdings grew from 28.91% to 35.68% [E43], driving positive institutional money flow [E44]. The reliance on a static DCF intrinsic value of Rs 724 [E45] ignores the operational reality of expanding operating margins reaching 17% in the TTM from 9% three years prior [E30] and management's reaffirmed EBIT margin target of 15% for FY27 [E75]. Furthermore, the bear's claim of an unsupported valuation overlooks the company's robust deal momentum, with last-12-month deal wins reaching $4,270 million, up 34.8% year-on-year [E88]. Finally, the negative margin of safety derived from models [E46] fails to account for a pristine balance sheet featuring nearly zero debt [E59], strong free cash flow of Rs 5,626 crore [E36], and a rules-based screen scoring a high 91 out of 100 [E63].

Conceded: TTM profit growth surged to 27% [E21] and net profit jumped 34% year-on-year [E66]. However, pointing to recent profit spikes ignores the longer-term structural stagnation where 3-year sales growth limps at 2% [E16] and 5-year profit growth sits at a meager 2% [E19]. While domestic institutions accumulated shares [E43], foreign institutional investors simultaneously reduced their stake from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42], indicating a notable exit of sophisticated global capital. The bull dismisses the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 724 [E45] as a static model, yet the reverse DCF reveals that today's elevated price already bakes in an aggressive 14.4% earnings growth expectation against a base case of just 2.0% [E47]. Finally, citing a pristine balance sheet and cash flows [E36, E59] does not justify a rich price-to-earnings multiple of 30.6x [E1] and price-to-book ratio of 5.88x [E2] that far exceed sector benchmarks of 19.6x and 1.95x [E6, E7].

Conceded: 3-year sales growth is 2% [E16] and 5-year profit growth is 2% [E19]. However, focusing solely on past stagnation ignores the sharp acceleration in the trailing twelve months, where sales grew 14% [E17] and profit surged by 27% [E21], alongside a 34% year-on-year net profit jump [E66]. While FII stakes moved from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42], domestic institutions aggressively expanded their ownership from 28.91% to 35.68% [E43], resulting in positive overall institutional money flow [E44]. The bear's reverse DCF concern regarding a 14.4% earnings expectation [E47] is entirely justified by management's track record and guidance, including a healthy order book with last-12-month deal wins up 34.8% to US$4,270 million [E88] and a reaffirmed full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% [E75]. Finally, the premium multiples of P/E 30.6x [E1] and P/B 5.88x [E2] are fully supported by superior operational efficiency, evidenced by an ROA of 11.42% versus a sector benchmark of 5.74% [E8] and an ROE of 18.62% against a sector benchmark of 10.38% [E9].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales grew 14% [E17], profit surged 27% [E21], and net profit jumped 34% YoY [E66]. However, the bull's attempt to dismiss multi-year stagnation ignores that 3-year sales growth is a meager 2% [E16] and 5-year profit growth is similarly stalled at 2% [E19], revealing a chronic pattern of long-term underperformance. While domestic institutions increased their holdings [E43], foreign institutional investors actively reduced their stakes from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42], indicating a substantial exit of sophisticated capital from the counter. Furthermore, claiming the 14.4% reverse DCF growth expectation [E47] is fully justified by order book metrics [E88] ignores the glaring structural disconnect highlighted by the negative margin of safety of -146.2% [E46] and an intrinsic valuation of Rs 724 against a price of Rs 1783 [E45]. Finally, while operational returns like ROA [E8] and ROE [E9] look strong relative to sector benchmarks, relying on them to justify a P/E of 30.6x [E1] and a P/B of 5.88x [E2] creates a dangerous valuation blind-spot where the current price already heavily discounts all future optimism [E69].
